TechArrayStudios · ThingMark

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 25 November 2026

This policy applies to the Android app ThingMark: Where Did I Put It? published by TechArrayStudios. ThingMark helps you remember where you stored your things: you take a photo of a box, drawer or shelf and note where it is. You do not need an account to use the app.

Summary

  • We do not require an account to use the app.
  • We do not run ads, analytics, or tracking in the app.
  • The app has no permission to use the internet, so it cannot send your data anywhere.
  • Your memories and photos stay on your device unless you choose to share them or save a backup.
  • We do not operate any servers for your data.

Information stored on your device

The app stores the following only on your phone, in app storage that other apps cannot read:

  • Photos you take or choose
  • The titles, places, spots, items, notes and photo pins you add
  • Lending notes you add (who has something and when it is due back). The app does not read your contacts.
  • App settings, such as whether you finished the intro and when you last made a backup (including the backup file’s name and folder)

This information is used only to run the app on that device.

Camera, photos and location

  • Camera: when you take a photo, the app opens your phone’s camera app. The app itself does not have camera permission.
  • Gallery: when you choose a photo, Android’s photo picker shares only the photo you select. The app cannot see the rest of your gallery.
  • Photo details: photos can contain hidden information, such as where they were taken. The app removes this information when it saves a photo.
  • Location: the app never asks for or uses your location.

Sharing, backups and restore (only if you choose)

  • Share: if you share a memory as an image, the app uses your device’s share feature. It goes only to the app you select. We do not receive a copy.
  • Save backup: you can save one backup file (.zip) with your memories and photos to your phone, using Android’s own “Save to” screen.
  • Send backup: you can send the backup file to another app you choose, such as Google Drive or email. That app then handles it under its own privacy policy.
  • Restore: you choose a backup file, or open one with ThingMark from another app. The app reads it on your device. We do not upload it anywhere.
  • Anyone with your backup file can see what is in it, so keep it somewhere private.

Android backup and moving to a new phone

ThingMark’s data is excluded from Android’s automatic cloud backup, so it is never uploaded to Google’s backup servers. When you set up a new phone by cable or Wi‑Fi transfer, Android can copy the app’s data directly from your old phone.

What we do not collect

  • We do not create user accounts on servers.
  • We do not collect your name, email address, photos or location.
  • We do not sell or rent personal data.
  • We do not use third-party advertising or analytics SDKs.
  • We do not track you across other apps or websites.

Purchases

The app currently has no in-app purchases. If we add an optional purchase later, payment will be handled entirely by Google Play and we will never receive your payment details. We will update this policy before that happens.

Children

ThingMark is not directed at children under 13 and collects no personal data from anyone.

Data retention and deletion

  • Your memories stay on your device until you delete them.
  • Deleted memories go to Trash and are permanently removed after 30 days, or sooner if you empty Trash.
  • Uninstalling the app removes all of its data from your device.
  • Backup files and shared images exist only where you saved or sent them. You can delete them there.

Changes

If this policy changes, we will update it and the date above. The current version is always in the app (Settings → Privacy policy) and at the link on ThingMark’s Google Play page.

Contact us
